Generated from the component evidence records — edit the records, not this page.

A component record answers questions about one part. These rules answer the ones that span several — whether a divider built from two resistors keeps a third part inside its own limit, whether a clamp event stays under everything downstream of it. Each rule is projected whole from stored evidence: its conditions, the exact facts it rests on, any conditioned arithmetic, and the exact wording of what it refuses to conclude.

## How to read these rules

- **The refusal is the rule.** — Every rule states, in its own words, what may NOT be concluded from the evidence above it. That sentence is the rule's real output; the verdict is shorthand for it.
- **A verdict belongs to the rule, not to a part.** — A rule's verdict says how far the cross-component question has been settled. It is never a judgement about any of the parts the rule names, and the verdicts are never combined into one.
- **Calculations are conditioned, and the conditions are the point.** — Each calculation publishes its expression, its inputs and the exact results that were recorded, together with the conditions under which the answer means anything. A result read without them is arithmetic mistaken for a measurement.
- **Numbers here were carried, not computed.** — The expressions are published so a reader can redo the arithmetic. This page does not evaluate them — the results shown are the ones the evidence recorded.
- **An evidence chain does not flow downhill.** — A stage being settled says nothing about any stage after it. A document confirming a limit is not a measurement of the assembled board.

## rule-rail-envelope

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-rail-envelope" />

**What this rule asks:** Whether every part on the input rail stays inside its own recorded limits across a legal power contract, a mis-contract, and a transient clamp event.

**Domain:** rail-envelope

**Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not certify regulated output or the 26.5 W rated total until all three outputs pass low-line, full-load, ripple and thermal tests with the programmed PD core.

**Conditions:** Current chain: Board P nominal 15 V / 3 A -> AP63201 +13.44 V, LM2596 +6.519 V and -14.145 V intermediates -> LT1963A +12/+5 V and adjustable LT3015 -12.054 V nominal. R5/R6 are 10.5 k/1 k 0.1%; tolerance/TCR/reference calculations are screening, with actual low-line dropout, ripple and thermal coupling open. Board A and original regulator facts are historical and are not current-stage proof. Prototype normal source envelope is15 V±5%,20 V unsupported; first power/programming uses5 V-only with B disconnected and retained15 V-only NVM readback before a PD-capable source.

## rule-tvs-clamp-vs-absmax

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-tvs-clamp-vs-absmax" />

**Domain:** tvs-clamp-vs-absmax

**Verdict:** UNSOURCED

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not certify surge survival or 20 V operation from 8/20 us table points, a static OVP bound or an assumed overshoot; measure connector, VBUS\_P, gate and rail transients, and keep the current 15 V Board B off a 20 V contract.

**Conditions:** Board P spec is the 20 V r3 draft (dec-p-20v-revision, dec-p-20v-front-end-r3, dec-p-front-end-r3-migration): D5 TVS2200DRVR C523793 clamps connector VBUS\_IN; Q3 CSD18543Q3A driven by the LM74700QDBVRQ1 C2941042 ideal-diode controller U3 (ANODE/EN on VBUS\_IN, CATHODE on EF\_IN) and U2 TPS16630PWPR C1849461 feed protected VBUS\_P, which carries STUSB4500 VDD, Q1 and Board B. The TPS26630 and Q4 B\_GATE pulldown of r2 are removed; the r2 arithmetic is archived. The Board P PCB is still the 15 V as-built SMAJ16A layout and is not re-synchronised. TVS2200 standoff (a DC maximum) is 22 V, 1.0 V above the 21.0 V project normal high (20 V +5 %); its clamp maximum is 28.0 V at 40 A 8/20 us 27 C and 28.35 V at 35 A 8/20 us 125 C. Board P Q1 is proposed as DMP3036SFG-7 C461081 (dec-p-20v-q1-5a; VDSS -30 V, VGSS +/-25 V), the same -30 V VDS as the AO3401A that remains on Board A and the as-built Board P PCB. That clamp point leaves 38.65 V to U2 IN/P\_IN 67 V and 31.65 V to Q3 VDS 60 V. Q3 VGS is bounded by U3: 13.9 V maximum charge-pump turn-off leaves 6.1 V to the 20 V VGS rating, and the 15 V GATE-ANODE absolute maximum leaves 5 V. C1 C13585 and C2 C14663 on VBUS\_IN are 50 V parts. The OVP trip maximum is 22.564238 V at initial tolerance and 22.671207 V with 25 ppm/C over 100 C (TPS16630 V(OVPR) 1.224 V maximum, the same row as the TPS26630); a slow connector overvoltage up to that trip overlaps the 22 V standoff but stays below the 24.6 V minimum breakdown, so D5 only leaks there. U2 keeps conducting for up to 14 us (OVP\_toff(dly) maximum) after a trip. The 2.53665 V hot-unplug overshoot is a project assumption without fact entries; it is eFuse let-through charge into the 80 uF VBUS\_P bulk, so it applies to VBUS\_P, not to the D5 connector node, giving 25.207857 V and 2.792143 V STUSB 28 V margin in the hot case. It rests on TYP rows (fast trip and I(SCP) have no tabulated maximum) and on a bulk ESR with no datasheet maximum, so no guaranteed VBUS\_P transient bound exists. STUSB limits keep their mirror-source trust limitation. The current Board B was screened for 15 V +/-5 % only; its 20 V coverage is not established. Output TVS/load limits and actual waveforms remain separate; the old SMAJ20A 32.4 V against U4 45 V comparison is explicitly retired and kept only as a labelled historical calculation. Phase 9 local clamps (dec-p-stusb-local-clamp): the STUSB4500 high-voltage pins no longer sit on VBUS\_P. VDD (U1.24) is fed through R29 1k + R30 470R (phase 10, dec-p-stusb-vdd-feed, 1.47 kOhm; was 2 x 1k) into VDD\_LOC with D9 BZT52C18-7-F C192739 and C38 1 uF; VBUS\_VS\_DISCH (U1.18) keeps R14 + R28 (now 2 x 1k) with D10 BZT52C20-7-F C260890 on the pin; DISCH (U1.9) sits behind R13 4.7k with D12 BZT52C18-7-F; VBUS\_EN\_SNK (U1.16) drives R12 through a Q6 BSS138 cascode whose gate is VDD\_LOC/2 (R31/R32 100k), with D11 BZT52C18-7-F on the pin. With VBUS\_P at the 28.35 V TVS2200 35 A / 125 C clamp row, the pin bound is the zener VZ maximum at IZT plus the TC maximum above 25 C, plus ZZT maximum times any current beyond IZT (a project linearisation, at most 3.65 mA and 0.16 V on VDD). The TC minimum of 12.4 mV/C (in the tc-max fact conditions) is positive, so a cold row is bounded by the 25 C VZ maximum. The pin bound is therefore 20.794 V on VDD and 23.0 V on VBUS\_VS\_DISCH at 125 C, under the 28 V limits. These local-clamp margins are scenario-conditioned: they assume VBUS\_P at the 28.35 V TVS2200 connector-node row, which this rule does not treat as a guaranteed VBUS\_P transient bound (see the overshoot discussion above); each pin margin holds for any VBUS\_P up to the voltage at which its clamp current would make VZ + ZZT x (I - IZT) reach 28 V. The STUSB 28 V pin limit therefore no longer bounds the main surge path; Q1 DMP3036SFG-7 VDS -30 V does (1.65 V at the 28.35 V row). The calc-p20-stusb-node-margin rows remain the unclamped reference.

**Conditions:** VDD\_LOC with D9 BZT52C18-7-F fed from VBUS\_P through R29 1k + R30 470R 1 % (1455.3 ohm minimum). STUSB limits keep their mirror-source trust limitation.

## rule-u4-inverting-stress

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-u4-inverting-stress" />

**Domain:** u4-inverting-stress

**Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not infer surge, startup or 20 V acceptance from normal DC margin or the static OVP bound; preserve the negative rail, floating ground and semiconductor stress calculations after every setpoint or source change.

**Conditions:** U4 local GND/ON-OFF/tab ride the renewed negative intermediate. The current Board B is a 15 V +/-5 % design: effective input and D3 reverse stress are VBUS plus negative magnitude, 29.145 V nominal and 30.564410 V at 15.75 V with the 14.814410 V hot/TCR screen. The 20 V Board P r3 draft bounds VBUS\_P at 22.564238 V (U2 TPS16630 OVP maximum, initial tolerance) and 22.671207 V with divider TCR over 100 C. With the hot/TCR negative screen U4 would see 37.485617 V, 2.514383 V below its 40 V operating limit; adding the 2.53665 V overshoot assumption gives -0.022267 V, so the operating limit is not maintained in that combined screen. Board B at 20 V input is not covered: AP63201, LDO dissipation, startup and the Board B limiter are unscreened. New D3 has 60 V reverse rating and maximum 0.52 V at 5 A/25C (0.45 V at 5 A/125C); use 0.52 V for the 25C conduction screen. C9 is 50 V. Reverse leakage is 0.5 mA maximum at 60 V/25C and 50 mA typical only at 60 V/125C; reverse-leakage heating is outside the forward-conduction model and requires qualification.

**Records this rule spans:**

- [`rec-lm2596s-adj-c347423`](/docs/components/records/lm2596s-adj-c347423/) — LM2596S-ADJ
- [`rec-c861077`](/docs/components/records/c861077/) — RT0603BRD0710K5L

## rule-ldo-dropout-chain

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-ldo-dropout-chain" />

**Domain:** ldo-dropout-chain

**Verdict:** UNSOURCED

**This rule refuses to conclude:** The new parts improve DC headroom, but mirror-source trust, full-temperature adjustment bias on both regulator types, actual low-line ripple, capacitor stability and coupled thermal behavior remain open.

**Conditions:** LT1963A replaces both positive regulators and adjustable LT3015 replaces the negative regulator, programmed by R26+R27 = 8.88 k over R28 = 1 k to nominal -12.054 V. AP pre-rail arithmetic is 13.219794..13.6624 V with the selected resistor/TCR envelope. Negative minimum is 13.483572 V with full-temperature reference and 0.35% combined resistor tolerance/TCR, leaving 0.433472 V above the 13.0501 V worst-case output-plus-dropout requirement before ripple. The LT3015 ADJ bias limit is specified at 25C only. LT1963A adjustment-bias maximum is only specified at 25C; do not extrapolate it as a full-temperature limit. Include load-dependent ground current in thermal screens and verify output capacitor ESR/effective capacitance.

## rule-q1-gate-drive-vs-contract

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-q1-gate-drive-vs-contract" />

**Domain:** q1-gate-drive-vs-contract

**Verdict:** UNSOURCED

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not program a 20 V PDO or certify the load switch from steady gate arithmetic, a static OVP bound or an assumed overshoot; the 20 V NVM image, readback, cable, Board B coverage and measured gate/source behaviour are all open.

**Conditions:** The as-built Board P PCB and the superseded dec-p-20v-q1-5a draft use 100 k source-to-gate/150 k gate-to-VBEN and source-referenced C35; in the 20 V draft Q1 source is the protected VBUS\_P node (after U3 LM74700/Q3 and U2 TPS16630 in r3). RESET is strapped to GND by R21 0 Ohm C21189 in r3 (r2 used 10 kOhm C17414); it sets no gate-drive polarity. Ideal asserted drive is -6 V at 15 V, -8 V at 20 V, -8.4 V at 21 V, -9.025695 V at the 22.564238 V OVP bound, -9.068483 V at the 22.671207 V hot/TCR bound and -10.083143 V with the 2.53665 V overshoot assumption, against the +/-25 V VGS rating of the proposed Q1 DMP3036SFG-7 C461081 (dec-p-20v-q1-5a), leaving 14.916857 V in the hot overshoot case; the as-built PCB and Board A keep the 12 V AO3401A. The 100 k/150 k rows above are the superseded dec-p-20v-q1-5a draft divider screened against the DMP3036SFG rating; the as-built PCB has the same divider but the 12 V AO3401A, which these rows do not screen. The phase-6 draft (dec-p-20v-q1-gate-clamp) changes the draft spec to R11 150 k (C22807) source-to-gate, R12 4.7 k (C23162) gate-to-VBEN and adds D8 BZT52C11-7-F (cathode VBUS\_P, anode Q1\_G): the open-clamp divider gives -4.605 V at 4.75 V, -4.848 V at 5 V and -5.090 V at 5.25 V, so the old -2.0 V threshold-band drive is gone, but the guaranteed DMP3036SFG 29 mOhm row is at -5 V, which this divider reaches only above about 5.157 V VBUS (-5.090 V at 5.25 V) and no divider can reach at 5.00 V nominal; 5 V conduction is in any case excluded by POWER\_ONLY\_ABOVE\_5V. From about 10.7 V up D8 conducts and holds |VGS| at 10.4-11.6 V (13.4 V minimum margin to 25 V); its current is about 3.08 mA at the 25.207857 V overshoot case, and VBEN sinks about 3.15 mA in total, D8 plus the 0.069 mA R11 share (the VBEN rating is UNSOURCED). With D8 open the divider alone reaches -24.442 V there, leaving 0.558 V, so D8 is required for margin, not optional. These steady numbers do not establish transient gate safety, and the asserted-low premise rests on the UNSOURCED VBEN fact, which bench work must confirm. The as-built PCB and NVM policy remain 15 V-only; no 20 V/5 A NVM image has been defined or read back, a 5 A e-marked cable is required, and the current Board B is not covered at 20 V. First power/programming must use a current-limited 5 V-only source with B disconnected; NVM programming, ordering and energizing need separate explicit permission. Verdict UNSOURCED (phase 6): the draft's clamp current must be sunk by VBEN, whose drive and sink rating rest on the UNSOURCED fact-stusb-vben, so the weakest input is unsourced before any bench question. Phase 10, with the phase-9 Q6 cascode (dec-p-stusb-local-clamp): R12 now ends on VBEN, the drain of Q6 BSS138-7-F C40912; its source is U1.16 (VBEN\_PIN, D11) and its gate is VG\_LOC = VDD\_LOC x 0.495-0.505 (R31/R32 100k C25803). The asserted rows above hold only if the Q6 drain-source drop at about 3.15 mA is small; the bundle has no BSS138 RDS(on) row (UNSOURCED). calc-p10-q6-vgs-margin keeps Q6 VGS 9.499 V inside the 20 V rating; calc-p10-q6-gate-drive-at-attach gives 0.665 / 0.583 V of overdrive at a 5 V attach (about 32 uA needed; POWER\_ONLY\_ABOVE\_5V keeps Q1 off there). Released, the pin sees at most VG\_LOC - VGS(th), about 10.5 V, and the Q6 drain up to VBUS\_P (28.35 V row) against its 50 V VDS (fact-c40912-vds); Q1 off-state integrity then depends on Q6 hot drain leakage, which is not in the bundle (UNSOURCED). The VBEN sink rating is UNSOURCED by absence: fact-stusb-vben records polarity and configuration only. The phase-7 C36/Q5/R27 soft-start network acts only while Q1 slews and is outside these steady rows. The verdict stays UNSOURCED; the weakest inputs are fact-stusb-vben and the missing Q6 RDS(on) and hot-leakage rows.

**Records this rule spans:**

- [`rec-umw-ao3401a-c347476`](/docs/components/records/umw-ao3401a-c347476/) — AO3401A
- [`rec-c25803`](/docs/components/records/c25803/) — 0603WAF1003T5E
- [`rec-c22807`](/docs/components/records/c22807/) — 0603WAF1503T5E

#### calc-renewal-q1-gate-voltage

<EvidenceAnchor id="calc-renewal-q1-gate-voltage" />

**Expression:** `-vbus_v * fact_c25803_resistance / (fact_c25803_resistance + fact_c22807_resistance)`

**Result:** `vgs_v`

**Conditions:** Ideal asserted open-drain low, capacitor/parasitic/time behaviour excluded. 15 V-only as-built rows plus 20 V draft rows at 20 V, the 21 V project normal high, the initial-tolerance OVP bound, the hot/TCR OVP bound, and the hot/TCR bound plus the overshoot assumption.

**Inputs:**

- [`fact-c25803-resistance`](/docs/components/records/c25803/#fact-c25803-resistance) on 0603WAF1003T5E
- [`fact-c22807-resistance`](/docs/components/records/c22807/#fact-c22807-resistance) on 0603WAF1503T5E

<EvidenceAnchor id="calc-p6-d8-clamp-current" />

#### calc-p10-q6-vgs-margin

<EvidenceAnchor id="calc-p10-q6-vgs-margin" />

**Expression:** `fact_c40912_vgs - vdd_loc_v * 0.505`

**Result:** `margin_v`

**Conditions:** Q6 gate at VDD\_LOC x R32 / (R31 + R32) with 1 % resistors (0.505 maximum ratio) and the source at about 0 V while U1.16 is asserted. vdd\_loc\_v rows: 20.38 V is the 105 C BZT52C18 VZ maximum at IZT without the ZZT excess term (19.1 V + 80 C x 16.0 mV/C), the continuous operating bound; 20.794 V is the 125 C surge-row pin bound of calc-p20-stusb-local-clamp-vdd (rule-tvs-clamp-vs-absmax).

#### calc-p10-q6-gate-drive-at-attach

<EvidenceAnchor id="calc-p10-q6-gate-drive-at-attach" />

**Expression:** `vdd_attach_v * 0.495 - fact_c40912_vgsth_max`

**Result:** `overdrive_v`

**Conditions:** Q6 gate overdrive at a 5 V attach with U1.16 asserted: VDD\_LOC minimum (VBUS 4.72 V, the 4.75 V vSafe5V minimum less a 0.03 V Q3/U2 drop (PA), less the 1.4847 kOhm feed drop at the stated IDD, scripts/pcb/calculate-input-ovp-20v.py) x 0.495 minimum divider ratio, minus the 1.5 V VGS(th) maximum (VDS = VGS, 250 uA, 25 C only). The current needed is about 32 uA; overdrive is not an RDS(on) bound.

**Inputs:**

- [`fact-c40912-vgsth-max`](/docs/components/records/c40912/#fact-c40912-vgsth-max) on BSS138-7-F

| vdd\_attach\_v | overdrive\_v       |
| -------------- | ------------------ |
| 4.373          | 0.6646350000000001 |
| 4.209          | 0.5834549999999998 |

## rule-inverting-startup-vs-pd-source

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-inverting-startup-vs-pd-source" />

**Domain:** inverting-startup-vs-pd-source

**Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not assume a3A charger starts the inverting stage because steady-state load is below its contract; capture the actual inrush and contract recovery.

**Conditions:** The retained manufacturer inverting-startup warning allows approximately 4.5 A for 2 ms or longer against a3A PD contract. The renewed negative bulk remains1410uF and stores about 0.141J at 14.145 V. Board P soft-start is not a demonstrated current limit; staged startup, actual adapter behavior and waveforms need qualification.

## rule-evidence-chain

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-evidence-chain" />

**What this rule asks:** How far each claim has travelled from a manufacturer document towards a measurement on real hardware, stage by stage.

**Domain:** source-to-bench-chain

**Verdict:** UNSOURCED

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not convert document, netlist or manufacturing checks into assembled, programmed or bench evidence; keep each unresolved downstream stage explicitly open.

**Conditions:** Board P routed geometry and current generated schematics have distinct evidence from incoming-part orientation, assembled boards, programmed NVM and measured behavior. ### Source-to-bench evidence chain

The stages a claim passes through, in order. A settled stage says nothing about any stage after it: a manufacturer document confirming a limit is not an inspection of the assembled board, and neither is a measurement. A stage with no facts against it is not one nobody got round to filling in: nothing has been established there yet, so the rule's conditions and its refusal above are the whole of what is known about it.

## rule-eurorack-output-harness

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-eurorack-output-harness" />

**Domain:** eurorack-output-harness

**Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not connect modules or certify polarity from a keyed housing alone; meter every rail through the actual cable and confirm solder process and loaded contact temperature before use.

**Conditions:** J10/J11 C4749189 replaces the old connector and guard. New pin groups1/2=-12 V,3..8=GND,9/10=+12 V,11/12=+5 V,13/14=CV,15/16=GATE. Doepfer pin1/red stripe convention is primary confirmed; imported numeric pad map, actual keyed cable continuity, finished-hole fit, wave solder compatibility and loaded contact temperature remain physical checks. Rail budgets are total board capacity shared by both outputs.

## rule-screw-output-harness

<EvidenceAnchor id="rule-screw-output-harness" />

**Domain:** eurorack-output-harness

**Verdict:** NEEDS BENCH

**This rule refuses to conclude:** Do not preserve old same-net links between the two new poles: that would short distinct rails. Do not certify18A per output from a terminal rating or visual model; verify polarity, wire retention, process, hole fit and loaded temperature within shared board targets.

**Conditions:** J6.1 GND/J6.2 -12V and J7.1 +5V/J7.2 +12V are separate poles. Retaining an old same-node Faston link would deterministically short distinct rails, not create an acceptable bench assumption. Whole-board targets +12V/1.2A,+5V/0.5A,-12V/0.8A are shared with J10/J11. The2.5A sum-of-magnitudes return screen adds no capacity; no18A per-output board claim is established. Mirrored UL15A/300V and IEC18A/250V ratings are conditional terminal ratings. Actual wire, torque, solder process,1.30mm finished-hole fit, loaded temperature and retention remain unverified. Model tails3.50mm do not establish physical4.50±.20mm tail clearance; use4.70mm conservative geometry and retain physical qualification as open.
